statement: Foundation Phase intentionally contains no novel experiments; future sessions must preserve this phase boundary until a human supplies Phase 2 authorization.

The primary Comellas-Yebra figure uses (x,0) as its first point, while the protected problems/heilbronn_n12/BASELINE.md says (0,0), creating zero triangle area for points 0,2,8. Source-faithful coordinates reproduce the exact 0.032598858691819698... baseline. Heilbronn search is blocked pending human amendment and a new foundation version.

The pinned evaluator and metric checkout are available at the exact upstream commit, but native Windows multiprocessing cannot re-import its dynamically loaded user_program module. No finite metric result was obtained; do not spend active search compute until a Linux-compatible runtime is available.

Clamping the published scope-112 witness to scope 111 gives a reproducible 100/105 unique-difference state with duplicate set [13,36,53,100,111]. Three 20-second single-mark simulated-annealing seeds did not leave this local basin, so single-mark retuning is not informative without multi-row or multi-mark moves.

From-scratch random Golomb-ruler sampling with 3000 candidates per level repeatedly dead-ended at four mutually disjoint rows after 0.684M-1.017M sampled rows per seed. Greedy irreversible choice is the dominant failure mode; a compatible-pool index and backtracking are needed before further random sampling.

Exhaustive radius-10 first-row replacement against fixed rows 1-6 found no compatible complete row at scope 111. The clamped witness's five conflicts cannot be resolved in that one-row neighborhood; this is local negative evidence only.

Two-mark and whole-row annealing across all seven rows also remained at 100/105 unique differences with duplicate set [13,36,53,100,111] for three seeds. More temperature tuning of this score is not justified without a new representation.

A radius-25 compatibility-pool search consumed each 30-second deadline saturating only 114-133 unique candidates for variable row 0; no other variable-row pools or DFS nodes were reached. Candidate-pool size must be bounded per row and search time allocated across rows.

OR-Tools 9.15.6755 CpSolver.solve crashes with a Windows access violation even on a three-variable AllDifferent control model. The scope-111 CP-SAT model produced no status or bound; this is runtime evidence only and should not be interpreted as infeasibility.

Upstream-inspired reversible block deletion improved pure-Python partial assembly from the prior four-row/60-difference greedy ceiling to five rows/75 unique differences for all three seeds, with 7,182-8,154 replacements per seed. No run completed seven rows or produced a validator-accepted scope-111 witness, so the gain is Level 1 proxy evidence only and active search is paused.

WSL2 Linux OR-Tools 9.15.6755 ran the unchanged exact scope-111 CP-SAT model without the native Windows access violation, but returned UNKNOWN after 120.147 seconds with no candidate or bound. Combined with Windows OR-Tools 9.12 and the tested redundant-propagation variant, the current direct formulation is low-yield for further short repeats; UNKNOWN is not mathematical infeasibility.

The exact pinned k-server taxi evaluator is operational in WSL2 with an external fork-start wrapper. The pinned parametrized example scores 17 violations, matching the upstream README's human-designed baseline; the separately reported 3-violation candidate is not included in the pinned checkout, so evaluator operation is verified but the 3 result is not reproduced.

Z3 5.1.0.0 ran the direct scope-111 integer Distinct model under WSL2 but returned unknown after 120.017 seconds with no candidate or bound. A second exact solver family did not resolve the current monolithic formulation; more direct solver churn is low-value.

Exhaustive radius-3 perturbation pools around all seven published rows contained 48,100 valid row masks. Exact compatibility DFS reached depth 5 before its 5,000,000-node cap, showing coordinated local repair has a larger search space than the one-row test but no complete witness.

Candidate-level CP-SAT exact-cover propagation over the same 48,100 radius-3 row masks returned UNKNOWN after 121.657 seconds with no assignment or bound. The finite neighborhood remains unresolved; this does not justify another short CP-SAT repeat.

A Glucose4 sequential-counter SAT encoding of the radius-3 candidate cover exceeded its 120-second wall budget without returning a status or artifact and was interrupted. The encoding is not a practical short-budget route in its current form; no satisfiability inference is made.

Twelve fixed-orientation SLSQP starts from the source-faithful Comellas-Yebra coordinates returned to the published minimum within float64 noise. No certified improvement or global negative result exists, and the protected transcription remains unusable for official comparison.

A 250,000-row deduplicated uniform catalog of valid scope-111 Golomb rulers, followed by rare-difference exact-cover branching, reached depth 4 before a 2,000,000-node cap. This matches the earlier global-greedy ceiling; uniform catalog expansion is low-value without a structural bias.

The pinned staged n=7 search reached its controller with a startup edge-order proxy in three local configurations: six fast plus three heavy workers caused a confirmed WSL global OOM; one fast plus three heavy workers failed with Wsl/Service/E_UNEXPECTED; one fast plus two heavy workers again made WSL unresponsive before any completed stage result. These runs provide no candidate evidence. Further local concurrency tuning is low-value without a more capable stable runtime or the missing reported 3-violation workspace.

A 100,000-mask library of individually valid scope-111 Golomb rulers did not pack into a complete DTS under either generic best-response swaps (96 unique differences) or explicit duplicate-conflict swaps (97 unique differences). Both states were rejected by the integer verifier. Valid-row library packing is low-yield without a new structural source of compatible masks.

The public FPGA-reference C search, adapted to n=7,k=5,M=111, completed separated training at TRAINING_M=152. Default persistence thresholds reached main search but repeatedly stalled at six rows; increasing the thresholds completed training but consumed the 120-second software budget before any main status. No candidate was decoded. This closes the bounded software reference family without an infeasibility claim; hardware-scale execution or a new structural construction is required.

Three new structured DTS families gave no target witness: affine gap coupling reached 89 unique differences, quadratic gap coupling reached 79, and exhaustive p=43 Ruzsa/Ling residue splitting completed 10,922,688 balanced transforms with best valid scope 195. These tested families should remain closed; this is not evidence of global DTS infeasibility.

For the pinned n=7 k-server Potential, the circle B cache is approximately 1001 x 279936 int32, about 1.12GB per process. The prior multi-worker staged configurations therefore duplicate a large cache and can exhaust the current WSL memory. A single-process/shared-cache architecture is a materially different runtime experiment; it does not change the evaluator or establish a k-server result.

A single-process architecture removed the prior cache-duplication failure: it built the 1001 x 279936 int32 circle cache and completed 700 exact circle candidates, including logged zero-violation circle milestones. However, one sequential full pinned taxi evaluation remained active past 1200 seconds and produced no violations_k score. The remaining bottleneck is full taxi potential evaluation, not worker initialization; further local concurrency tuning is low-value.

A screen that eliminated all five known violations of the independently reproduced 5-violation seed selected coefficient-8 mutations that scored 348,550 violations on the full taxi metric. Fixed-edge repair is therefore not a valid global selector for the canonical potential family; newly introduced violations dominate. Future local search must use a global screen or exact full metric.
